content: Sida cordifolia, commonly referred to as Country Mallow or Bala, is a herbaceous plant belonging to the Malvaceae family. It is extensively utilized in Ayurvedic medicine. This plant typically grows in transitional or waste areas. Its leaves are heart-shaped, with one leaf present at each node, and its flowers, which are yellow in color, are produced at the growing ends of the plant. The herb is characterized by its cooling, astringent, and intensely bitter properties, which make it effective in reducing inflammation. It also exhibits diuretic and invigorating effects. In Ayurvedic terms, Sida cordifolia is particularly beneficial for conditions associated with deranged Pitta dosha. It is known to rejuvenate the nervous, circulatory, and urinary systems. The root of Sida cordifolia has been used for over 2,000 years in the treatment of asthma and arthritis. Cooked leaves of the plant are traditionally used as a remedy for piles. In Cambodia, the roots are considered to have diuretic and depurative properties and are employed in the treatment of gonorrhea and ringworm. Bala is also incorporated into massage oils, which are applied topically to alleviate sore muscles and joints in conditions such as arthritis, rheumatism, sciatica, and neuritis of the legs. The leaves of Sida cordifolia can be prepared as an infusion to treat fevers and delirium. The root of the plant is astringent, diuretic, and tonic, and its infusion is used in the management of cystitis, strangury, hematuria, bleeding piles, chronic dysentery, leucorrhea, and gonorrhea. The seeds of the plant are considered aphrodisiac and nervine and are used in the treatment of colic, tenesmus, and gonorrhea. The plant contains several active constituents, including ephedrine (approximately 1%), phytosterols, and potassium nitrate. The phytosterols may exert an estrogenic effect. Sida cordifolia is included in some weight-loss supplements, particularly as a substitute following the ban on ephedra. These supplements, which contain 1% ephedrine alkaloid, are often used by bodybuilders and athletes to promote fat loss, enhance performance, and achieve a leaner physique. The supplements are commonly manufactured in tablet form, often combined with caffeine. The effects of Sida cordifolia on the body differ from those of Ma Huang, a warmer herb and a well-known but controversial ephedra extract. Like its relatives (Ma Huang and pseudoephedrine), Sida cordifolia is effective as an anti-asthmatic treatment. However, it is more suitable for individuals with a hot constitution rather than those with a cold constitution. The plant is also considered diaphoretic, diuretic, and a stimulant of the central nervous system. Sida cordifolia is native to India, Cambodia, and Sri Lanka.
